title: Reading the result: the teaching bands
objectives: Read an overlap figure with the under-30 / 30–50 / over-50 bands.
Say when high overlap is acceptable anyway.
body_md:
Reading the result (rule of thumb, not a regulation): under 30% — funds are genuinely different; fine to hold both. 30–50% — meaningful common core; ask what each fund adds. Over 50% — largely the same portfolio; consider keeping one.

| Overlap between two funds | What it usually means | Typical response |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Under 30% | Funds are genuinely different | Fine to hold both |
| 30–50% | Meaningful common core | Ask what each fund adds |
| Over 50% | Largely the same portfolio | Consider keeping one |

Bands are an internal teaching guide. Use judgement: two index funds on different indices can overlap heavily and still have a clear role each.
example: Two funds at 55% overlap: largely the same portfolio — consider keeping one, unless each has a clear distinct role.
say: Under 30%: genuinely different. Over 50%: consider keeping one.
Bands are a teaching guide, not a regulation.
never: Over 50% overlap always means sell immediately.
